ukberi-tibyan:1-2.t:
[Translator's note: the entry opens with a detached line, apparently a marginal gloss on «قُرَيْش»:] It is a diminutive of truncation (taṣghīr al-tarkhīm), because «الْقَرْش» is gathering, and the agent noun is «قَارِش», so by analogy [its diminutive] would be «قُوَيْرِش»; it was truncated and made diminutive.
Allah the Exalted said: (لِإِيلَافِ قُرَيْشٍ (١) إِيلَافِهِمْ رِحْلَةَ الشِّتَاءِ وَالصَّيْفِ (٢)).
The «lām» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the words of the Exalted (فَلْيَعْبُدُوا), i.e. let them worship Allah the Exalted because of their familiarity, and the [fāʾ] does not prevent that.
It is also said that it is attached to «جَعَلَهُمْ» in the preceding sūra, because the two are like a single sūra.
It is also said that the implied form is: «اعْجَبُوا لِإِيلَافٍ» (marvel at the familiarity). There are [several] readings of it. The first: «إِلْف», which is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «أَلِفَ يَأْلَفُ». The second: «إِلَاف», like «كِتَاب» and «قِيَام». The third: «إِيلَاف», whose verb is «آلَفَ» with a long vowel.
The fourth: «إِئْلَاف», with two hamzas, produced according to the original form; it is anomalous (shādhdh) in usage [and in analogy]. The fifth: with a hamza bearing kasra, followed by a vowelless yāʾ, followed by a hamza bearing kasra; this is far-fetched, and its justification is that the reader lengthened the kasra so that the yāʾ arose, intending thereby to separate the two hamzas, like the alif in «أَأَنْذَرْتَهُمْ».
(إِيلَافِ) is a badal (substitute) for the first. (رِحْلَةَ) is governed by the maṣdar.

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِي أَطْعَمَهُمْ مِنْ جُوعٍ وَآمَنَهُمْ مِنْ خَوْفٍ (٤)).
The words of the Exalted (مِنْ جُوعٍ) and (مِنْ خَوْفٍ): i.e. because of hunger.
It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. He fed them while they were hungry. And Allah knows best.
